q: 1. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circle
explain: In left-to-right network flow diagramming, the task on the left precedes and must be completed before downstream tasks.

q: 2. The first method invented for planning projects, was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart) method, invented in the late 1800s, was the earliest project planning tool, preceding milestone charts, CPM, and PERT.

q: 3. PERT is
explain: PERT is event oriented, since its network is analysed in terms of events.

q: 4. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis uses all three time estimates - optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely - to compute the expected activity duration.

q: 5. CPM is
explain: CPM is activity oriented.

q: 6. The performance of a specific task in CPM, is known
explain: In CPM, the performance of a specific task is termed an activity.

q: 7. PERT adopts
explain: PERT uses three time estimates and probability, so it is probabilistic.

q: 8. Completion of an activity on CPM network, is generally known
explain: In CPM networks, the point of completion (or start) of an activity is represented as a node.

q: 9. CPM adopts
explain: CPM uses a single fixed time estimate, so it is deterministic.

q: 10. The artificial activity which indicates that an activity following it, cannot be started unless the preceding activity is complete, is known as
explain: A dummy activity is an artificial, zero-duration link used to enforce correct dependency/precedence relationships in the network.

q: 11. Which of the following statements is true?
options: PERT is activity oriented and adopts deterministic approach
CPM is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
CPM is activity oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
PERT is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
explain: PERT is event oriented and probabilistic. CPM is activity oriented and deterministic.

q: 12. In a time-cost optimization using CPM the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: To reduce project duration most economically, we crash the critical activity that has the lowest cost slope (cheapest to crash first).

q: 13. A dummy activity
options: is represented by a dotted line
explain: A dummy activity is artificially introduced, shown as a dotted arrow, and consumes no time - all characteristics apply.

q: 14. When the events are numbered in a network then the number of the head event of an activity is
options: always larger than the number of the tail event of same activity
always smaller than the number of the tail event of the same activity
always equal to the number of the tail event of the same activity
explain: By Fulkerson's rule, the head event number is always greater than the tail event number.

q: 15. The amount of time required performing any event in case of PERT should be ................... CPM.
explain: Because PERT deals with uncertain/probabilistic time estimates and CPM uses deterministic ones, the actual time required can vary based on the nature of the project.

q: 16. The estimated time required to perform an activity, is known as
explain: Duration is the estimated time needed to complete an activity.

q: 17. PERT technique of network analysis is useful for
explain: PERT is ideally suited for Research and Development projects where the duration of activities is uncertain and has not been performed before.

q: 18. The difference between the time available to do a job and the time required to do the job, is known as
explain: Float (slack) is defined as the difference between available time and required time for completing an activity.

q: 19. Latest start of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The latest start time of an activity must be less than or equal to the latest allowable event time at its preceding node to avoid delaying the project.

q: 20. PERT means
options: pertinent programming related to a project
explain: PERT is the standard acronym for Program Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 21. The critical activity has
explain: By definition, a critical activity has zero total float, since any delay would push back the overall project completion.

q: 22. PERT is
explain: PERT focuses on milestones or 'events' (reaching a specific stage), whereas CPM focuses on the 'activities' or tasks themselves.

q: 23. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as
explain: Free float is the amount of delay possible in an activity without affecting the earliest start of any succeeding activity.

q: 24. Earliest finish of an activity is always
options: greater than earliest event time of the following node
less than earliest event time of the following node
less than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
greater than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
explain: The following node's earliest time is the maximum of the earliest finishes of all activities entering it, so EF ≤ it.

q: 25. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents
explain: The critical path determines the minimum time in which the entire project can be completed.

q: 26. Select the incorrect statement
options: earliest start of an activity is the early event time of the node it leaves
latest finish of an activity is the late event time of the node it enters
latest start of an activity is its latest finish minus its duration
explain: All three statements are correct, so 'none of the above' is the answer.

q: 27. Which one of the following represents an activity
explain: All listed tasks (curing concrete, setting a question paper, preparing breakfast) are processes that take time and resources, hence all represent activities.

q: 28. If the optimistic time, most likely time and pessimistic time for activity A are 4, 6 and 8 respectively and for activity B are 5, 5.5 and 9 respectively, then
options: expected time of activity A is greater than the expected time of activity B
expected time of activity B is greater than the expected time of activity A
expected time of both activities A and B are same
explain: tE(A) = (4+24+8)/6 = 6 and tE(B) = (5+22+9)/6 = 6, so they are equal.

q: 29. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' denotes a completed state/milestone (an instantaneous occurrence), representing an event rather than an ongoing process.

q: 30. If an activity has its optimistic, most likely and pessimistic times as 2, 3 and 7 respectively, then its expected time and variance are respectively
31. Critical path lies along the activities having total float
explain: Activities on the critical path always have zero total float by definition.

q: 32. Select the incorrect statement
options: start float and finish float are always equal
total float can be either start float or finish float
start float and finish float need not be equal
start float and finish float are the differences between activity times and not event times
explain: Per the answer key, c. Note: standard theory says start and finish float are equal for an activity, so the key looks questionable.

q: 33. The benefit of the PERT network is taken by the management in
options: readjusting the time to meet the target
explain: PERT provides a comprehensive framework for scheduling, inter-departmental coordination, and dynamic readjustment based on probability.

q: 34. The time which result in the least possible construction cost of an activity, is known
explain: (May be wrong )As per book Normal time is the duration at which the activity's direct cost is minimum (most economical execution pace).

q: 35. Which of the following time estimate is related to PERT?
explain: PERT uses a 'three-time estimate' approach (Optimistic, Pessimistic, and Most Likely) to account for uncertainty.

q: 36. If t0, tp and tm are the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates of an activity respectively, the expected time t of the activity will be
explain: The PERT expected time formula is te = (t0 + 4tm + tp)/6, giving greatest weight to the most likely time.

q: 37. The event which act as head as well as tail for different activities is, called
explain: An internal node in a network that marks the finish of one activity and the start of another is a dual role event.

q: 38. The figure below is used to indicate (merge symbol where multiple arrows converge into one node)
explain: When multiple activity arrows converge into a single node, this is called a merge event.

q: 39. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using the PERT formula $t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6$: $(1 + 4(3) + 11) / 6 = 24 / 6 = 4$ days.

q: 40. The figure below is used to indicate (burst symbol where one node diverges into multiple arrows)
explain: When a single node diverges into multiple activity arrows, this is called a burst event.

q: 41. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time is
explain: At the expected time Z = 0, so the probability is 50%.

q: 42. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known
explain: Critical ratio scheduling is the specific technique used to set and maintain job priorities based on time remaining versus work remaining.

q: 43. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis relies on all three time estimates to calculate the expected mean time.

q: 44. PERT is
options: used for research and development projects
based on three time estimates for activities linking up two events
explain: PERT is event-oriented, commonly used for R&D projects with uncertain durations, and relies on three time estimates linking events - all statements are true.

q: 45. In resources levelling
options: total duration of project is increased
uniform demand of resources is achieved
explain: Resource levelling aims at a uniform demand for resources, and may extend the project duration.

q: 46. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Events are graphically represented as circles or rectangles, commonly referred to as nodes in a network diagram.

q: 47. CPM is
options: is built of activities oriented programme
explain: CPM synthesizes project activities into an integrated program, is activity-oriented, and suits repetitive construction-type work - all apply.

q: 48. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time in PERT is
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) in a normal distribution represents the 50% probability mark (the mean).

q: 49. CPM family includes
explain: The CPM family of techniques includes Critical Path Analysis, Critical Path Plotted diagrams, and Critical Path Scheduling variants - all the above.

q: 50. The slack for an event i is given by
explain: Event slack is given by the difference between latest allowable time and earliest expected time[cite: 1].
